_about: Money patch round (R3): money values, savings requirements, text fixes.

scenarios.title: Your First Real Payday
scenarios.text: Your first real paycheck lands, and it has more zeros than {parent} made in a year. Your phone starts buzzing before you've finished reading the number.

choices.label: Save most of it
choices.result: You put most of it into an account you promise not to touch and buy one thing: a mattress that isn't from a dorm. It's dull, and you sleep very well.

choices.label: Spend it like you earned it
choices.result: You buy the car, the watch and dinner for the whole rookie class. It feels incredible for about a month.

choices.label: Pay off {parent}'s debts
choices.result: {parent} refuses twice when you ask for the number on every bill, then gives in the third time. The calls home sound different after that: lighter, and a lot longer.

choices.label: Split it the way you always have
choices.result: You do what you did with your first paycheck at sixteen, just with more zeros: a third saved, a third home, a third yours. It's an old habit, and it holds.
choices.lock_text: having handled your first paychecks wisely

scenarios.title: Where You Live
scenarios.text: Half the roster lives in the same glass tower downtown, with a rooftop pool and a doorman who knows everyone's name. The rent is a quarter of your salary.

choices.label: Rent something modest
choices.result: You rent a two-bedroom twenty minutes from the facility, above a bakery. The teammates call it 'the bakery'. You save more in a month than some of them save in a year, and the commute is short.

choices.label: Move into the tower
choices.result: The lease in the tower gets signed on a Tuesday. The pool parties are legendary and the elevators are full of teammates, and the rent comes out of every check like a tax.

choices.label: Room with a teammate
choices.result: Splitting a place with another rookie is cheaper and louder than you planned. You never eat dinner alone, and you learn more about him than you ever wanted to.

scenarios.title: The Coach for Hire
scenarios.text: A private kicking coach who rebuilt three pro careers offers you his whole offseason: his field, his methods, his famous temper. The price is a number your agent repeats twice.

choices.label: Hire him for the summer
choices.result: The summer belongs to him: brutal drills at dawn, video at night, a temper that softens by July. Your leg feels new by August, and you've never been so tired.

choices.label: Stay with the club's staff
choices.result: The club's staff knows your body, so you stay. It's less glamorous and steady, and the trainers quietly appreciate the vote of confidence.

choices.label: Take most of the summer off
choices.result: Most of the summer, off: lake, family, sleep. You come back rested, a little rusty, and happier than you've been in a long time.

choices.label: Check his record first
choices.result: Two of his former clients, called before you decide. Both rave about the results and warn you about the temper. You hire him with your eyes open, and it shows.

scenarios.title: The Incentive Clause
scenarios.text: Your contract pays a bonus if you hit ninety percent this season, and your agent keeps texting you the math: where you are, what's left, what one miss would mean.

choices.label: Ask your agent to stop
choices.result: No more math, please, you text back. You'll find out at the end of the season, and the next three months are quieter.

choices.label: Chase the number
choices.result: The number goes on your locker, and you chase it every practice. It's motivating, and some nights it's all you can think about.

choices.label: Forget the bonus
choices.result: Forgotten, on purpose, and the agent's texts go unread. If it comes, it comes, and you kick more freely than you have in years.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Discount
scenarios.text: The club offers less than the market and asks you to take it because 'you're family here'. The general manager says it twice, and puts his hand on your shoulder the second time.

choices.label: Take the discount
choices.result: The discount, accepted. The club remembers it, and so does the locker room, and you never quite know if it was generous or foolish.

choices.label: Meet in the middle
choices.result: The middle ground, found by your agent over two weeks of calls. Everyone is a little unhappy and fine, which your agent says is how you know it's fair.

choices.label: Test the market next spring
choices.result: Next spring's open market, it is. You kick like it all year, and every practice feels like an audition for twenty-nine other clubs.

scenarios.title: The Big Check
scenarios.text: Your signing bonus clears on a Tuesday. Within an hour your phone lights up with cousins, a car dealer, two realtors and someone from high school who wants to 'catch up'.

choices.label: Put it somewhere boring
choices.result: You put almost all of it somewhere boring and tell everyone it's tied up. Nobody believes you, and nobody can get to it.

choices.label: Celebrate properly
choices.result: The whole family, on a trip, and then the house with the pool. It's the best summer anyone in your family has had, and the pool bill arrives in September.

choices.label: Set aside a family share
choices.result: You set aside one share for family and tell them it's the only one. The cousins grumble. {parent} quietly approves.

scenarios.title: The Honest Advisor
scenarios.text: A financial advisor recommended by your long snapper walks you through a plan so boring it's almost funny: index funds, a budget, a rule about cars.

choices.label: Hire the boring advisor
choices.result: You hire the advisor and follow the rule about cars, mostly. Nothing exciting happens to your money, which is the point.

choices.label: Ask for more upside
choices.result: More upside, you say. The advisor says no, explains why in plain words and doesn't budge. You hire them anyway, partly because they wouldn't budge.

choices.label: Pass for now
choices.result: You say you'll think about it and never call back. The money sits in a checking account doing nothing at all.

scenarios.title: The Missing Money
scenarios.text: Your bank calls on a Tuesday morning: a transfer you didn't authorize, the third one this year. The advisor with the boat isn't answering, and his office number goes to a recording.

choices.label: Call a lawyer before practice
choices.result: You make the calls in the parking lot. By Friday the accounts are frozen, a forensic accountant is on it, and you know the number: four of every ten dollars you've earned.

choices.label: Call {parent}
choices.result: You call {parent} and say the number out loud. He's quiet for a long time, then tells you about the year he lost his job and what he did the next morning. You write it all down.

choices.label: Keep it quiet and fix it yourself
choices.result: You tell nobody, including the three teammates he also manages. You tell them everything's fine, which is a lie, and spend the season doing math in the training room.

choices.label: Call your agent first
choices.result: Your agent has seen this before. Within an hour you have a lawyer, an accountant and a plan, and a warning to call the other three players he manages before the news does.
choices.lock_text: having hired an agent who tells you the truth

scenarios.title: The Lawsuit
scenarios.text: Your lawyer says you can sue the advisor who took your money. It'll take three years, cost a fortune in fees, and your name will be in every story about it.

choices.label: Sue him
choices.result: You file. The case drags on for years, you testify twice, and some of the money comes back long after you've stopped counting on it.

choices.label: Report him and move on
choices.result: You file the report with the regulators and let them handle it. He's barred from the business a year later. You never see a dime.

choices.label: Join with the other players
choices.result: You call the three teammates he also handled. Together you hire one lawyer and split the bill. It's slower, and nobody faces it alone.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant
scenarios.text: An old college teammate wants your name and your money on a steakhouse downtown. He has a chef, a location and a business plan he wrote last night, and he keeps saying 'can't miss.'

choices.label: Put your money in
choices.result: You sign the papers at his kitchen table. Your name goes up in lights in March, and you eat there twice a week because it's yours.

choices.label: Ask to see real numbers
choices.result: A real plan, the lease and an accountant's review, please. He's offended, sends half of it, then stops answering. You keep your money and lose some of a friendship.

choices.label: Lend your name, not your money
choices.result: The opening night, a photo line and nothing more: your name, not your money. He's disappointed and says so, then takes the deal.

choices.label: Send it to your advisor
choices.result: Your advisor reads the plan in an afternoon and circles four things that would sink it. You send the list to your old teammate as a favor. He fixes two of them and opens without you.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant Is Failing
scenarios.text: The steakhouse is losing money every week. The chef quit, your old teammate isn't answering, and your name is still lit up over the door.

choices.label: Close it now
choices.result: You close it, pay the staff two weeks' wages from your own pocket and take your name down yourself. It hurts, and it's over.

choices.label: Put more money in
choices.result: Another check, to keep it open one more season. The food gets better, the reviews get kinder, and the losses don't change at all.

choices.label: Sell your share to your partner
choices.result: You sell your share to your old teammate for whatever he can pay. You lose most of it and keep the friendship, barely.

choices.label: Let your advisor run the exit
choices.result: Your advisor finds a buyer for the lease and the equipment within a month. You lose money, but a lot less than you would have.

scenarios.title: The Car Dealership
scenarios.text: A car dealership wants you as a partner: your face on the billboards, your money in the lot, and a guaranteed parking space with your name on it.

choices.label: Become a partner
choices.result: You sign. Your face goes up on the highway, and every teammate calls you about a deal. The dealership's books are the dealer's business, until they aren't.

choices.label: Do the ads, skip the ownership
choices.result: You agree to the billboards for a flat fee and keep your money out of the lot. It's less exciting and a lot safer.

choices.label: Keep your name off the lot
choices.result: No dealership, no billboard, no parking space. Your money stays where it is, and the dealership signs a weatherman, whose face you see every day.

scenarios.title: The Friend's Start-Up
scenarios.text: {best_friend} is starting a company, a real one with a plan, a lawyer and two hires, and asks you over dinner to be the very first investor. They've practiced the pitch.

choices.label: Invest
choices.result: You write the check because it's {best_friend}, and because the plan is actually good. You get a seat at their first board meeting and don't understand half of it.

choices.label: Invest a little, and say why
choices.result: You invest a small piece and tell {best_friend} why it's small. It stings for a day, and they respect it after that.

choices.label: Say no as a friend
choices.result: You say you don't mix friendship and money, and you mean it kindly. {best_friend} says they understand, and calls a little less often.

scenarios.title: The Start-Up Calls
scenarios.text: {best_friend}'s company is close: one more check and they make it to the next stage, or they fold this month. They call you late at night, trying hard not to ask.

choices.label: Write the last check
choices.result: You write it. Six months later the company is bought, and your share turns into the best investment of your life. {best_friend} cries on the phone.

choices.label: Hold the line
choices.result: You don't put in more. The company makes it anyway with someone else's money, and your share is smaller than it could have been. You're still glad for them.

choices.label: Help them find another investor
choices.result: Two people from the owner's gala, introduced to {best_friend} by you over coffee. One of them writes the check within a week.

choices.label: Ask your advisor to look first
choices.result: Your advisor reads the numbers and says this one is real. You write the check with your eyes open, and it pays.

scenarios.title: The Tax Letter, Pro
scenarios.text: You owe taxes in every state where you played a road game, and your old accountant didn't file most of them. The letters have started to arrive.

choices.label: Hire a sports accountant
choices.result: You hire an accountant who does nothing but athletes. It takes a month of paperwork and a painful check, and it's done.

choices.label: Ignore the letters
choices.result: The letters go in a drawer. They come back with penalties, then with a lawyer's name on the envelope, and every one of them makes your stomach drop.

choices.label: Ask the veterans at lunch
choices.result: Every veteran at the lunch table has a horror story and a phone number. You call the one who sounds least scary, and she fixes it in a month.

choices.label: Pay it from the account you never touch
choices.result: You pay it from the account you've never touched since your first paycheck. It's a big number, and it doesn't keep you up at night.
choices.lock_text: having handled money carefully since your first paycheck

scenarios.title: Family Asks for Money
scenarios.text: {sibling} needs money, a real amount, and doesn't want {parent} to know. They call late, after the kids are asleep, and apologize three times before they say the number.

choices.label: Help, and keep the secret
choices.result: You send the money quietly and keep the secret. {sibling} pays you back slowly over two years, a little every month, and never forgets that you didn't ask any questions.

choices.label: Help, with a plan
choices.result: You help, with conditions: an advisor, a budget, a plan written down. {sibling} grumbles and agrees, and it works well enough that they never need to call you like that again.

choices.label: Ask them to tell {parent}
choices.result: You gently ask them to tell {parent}. They do, eventually, after a hard week, and the family solves it together, slowly, around the same table where all the big things get solved.

scenarios.title: The Cousin Nobody Remembers
scenarios.text: Someone from your hometown with your last name, a folder of drawings and a business idea is waiting by your car after practice. He says you met at a wedding when you were nine.

choices.label: Hear the pitch, then check it
choices.result: You listen, take the paperwork and have your agent look at it. The idea is real; the numbers aren't. You say no with reasons.

choices.label: Buy him lunch, not the idea
choices.result: You buy him lunch and talk about family for an hour. You don't invest, and he leaves happier than he came.

choices.label: Say no before he finishes
choices.result: No, before he's finished his first sentence, and you get in your car. It's quick and a little cold, and {parent} hears about it from three relatives by Sunday.

scenarios.title: {parent}'s House
scenarios.text: You could pay off {parent}'s mortgage this week with one transfer. He's told you not to, twice, in the voice he used when you were twelve.

choices.label: Do it anyway
choices.result: You pay it off and tell him after. He's furious for an hour and doesn't speak at dinner. A month later, he still has the letter from the bank on his fridge.

choices.label: Ask what he'd accept
choices.result: You ask {parent} what he would actually accept. He agrees to a loan with no interest, insists on paying it back, and pays it back early.

choices.label: Respect his wish
choices.result: You respect his wish and let it go. He's proud of that, in his quiet way, and you send money to his church instead.

choices.label: Do it the way that worked before
choices.result: You set it up the way you did last time: quietly, through the bank, with his name on everything. He grumbles and signs.
choices.lock_text: having helped your family with money before

scenarios.title: The Foundation
scenarios.text: Your charity foundation's director is spending more on galas than on kids: the books show a ballroom, a band and a photographer, and only two new programs all year.

choices.label: Replace the director
choices.result: A new director, hired by you after a hard conversation with the old one. You run the next year closely, and the programs double.

choices.label: Audit the books
choices.result: An outside audit, every line, with new rules on spending afterward. The director stays, chastened, and the money starts reaching kids.

choices.label: Trust the director
choices.result: The galas raise money too, you tell yourself, and you let it run. The next annual report is glossy and thin.

scenarios.title: The Watch, the Car, the Chain
scenarios.text: The locker room has a dress code nobody wrote down: the watch, the car, the chain. It costs about what you made as a rookie.

choices.label: Keep up
choices.result: You buy the watch and the car. You look the part, and every month the statement looks a little worse.

choices.label: Opt out with a joke
choices.result: The same old truck shows up every day, and you call it 'retro'. It becomes a running joke in the locker room, and nobody actually minds; one rookie copies you.

choices.label: Ask a veteran who went broke
choices.result: The oldest player on the roster takes his watch off when you ask about it, sets it on the table and tells you what it cost him in the end.

scenarios.title: Broke in Your Thirties
scenarios.text: The money's gone faster than the career. There's a mortgage, a family, a car payment, and maybe three seasons left in your leg, if you're very lucky.

choices.label: Make a hard plan
choices.result: An honest advisor and a hard plan: a smaller house, no new cars, a budget taped to the fridge. It hurts, and it works.

choices.label: Tell your family everything
choices.result: You tell your family everything at the kitchen table. It's the worst conversation of your life and the best one; nobody leaves.

choices.label: Kick for one more contract
choices.result: You decide to kick for one more contract like your family depends on it. It does, and every practice feels heavier.

scenarios.title: The Pension Meeting
scenarios.text: The players' union holds a meeting about pensions and retirement plans in a hotel conference room. Six players show up, and you're the youngest by four years.

choices.label: Go and take notes
choices.result: Notes on everything, for two hours. It's boring and important, and you understand your pension for the first time in your career.

choices.label: Bring twelve teammates next time
choices.result: Twelve teammates at the next meeting, recruited by you one at a time. The union rep looks at you like you've performed a miracle.

choices.label: Skip it
choices.result: Retirement feels far away, so you skip it. The six who went start a group chat, and you're not in it.

scenarios.title: The Card Game
scenarios.text: The card game in the back of the team plane has a buy-in bigger than your first car, and the veterans running it have saved you the seat by the window. The flight is four hours long.

choices.label: Put the headphones on
choices.result: Headphones on, seat back, and four hours of sleep while the shouting carries on behind you. You land rested, and nobody says a word about it the next morning.

choices.label: Sit up front with the specialists
choices.result: Up front with the snapper and {holder}, a crossword and a bag of pretzels. It's the quietest flight of the season, and the three of you finish the puzzle.

choices.label: Take the seat
choices.result: The window seat is yours for the flight. By the time the wheels touch down you owe a veteran more than your signing bonus, and the team's security director has heard about the game by lunch.

choices.label: Text your advisor a photo of the stakes
choices.result: You text your advisor a photo of the buy-in, and the reply comes back in four words: absolutely not, go sleep. You laugh, and you do exactly that.
choices.lock_text: with an honest advisor in your corner

scenarios.title: The Team Fine
scenarios.text: The club fines you and calls you in. {coach} is in the room, and so is the general manager, who has a folder with your name on it.

choices.label: Own it
choices.result: You don't explain it away. You say what happened, what you'll change and who can hold you to it. The general manager closes the folder early.

choices.label: Explain it away
choices.result: You explain why it wasn't really your fault. The general manager listens to all of it and writes one word at the top of the page.

choices.label: Say you've been here before
choices.result: You tell them you've sat in a room like this in college and what you did after. {coach} nods slowly. The fine stands. The tone changes.

scenarios.title: League Discipline
scenarios.text: The league office wants a meeting about the strike on your record. It isn't a conversation; it's a hearing, in a gray room, with a lawyer from the players' union at your side.

choices.label: Accept the suspension
choices.result: You accept two games and don't appeal. You practice with the scout team, and the veterans notice that you show up every day anyway.

choices.label: Fight it
choices.result: You appeal and say the league is making an example of you. The appeal fails, the suspension stands, and now the whole league knows your name for the wrong reason.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Minimum
scenarios.text: You're on the veteran minimum, a third of what you made in your prime. The rookie at the next locker drives your old car; he bought it from the dealer you sold it to.

choices.label: Laugh about it with him
choices.result: Laughing about it together, at the lockers. He offers to sell it back to you at a discount, and you decline, and it becomes your running joke.

choices.label: Adjust the budget
choices.result: A smaller budget, built at the kitchen table, and nobody in the house misses the things you cut. You're surprised how little you needed.

choices.label: Kick for the next deal
choices.result: Every practice, like the next deal depends on it, because it does. It's motivating, and on bad days it's heavy.

scenarios.title: The Divorce
scenarios.text: The lawyers have the paperwork ready on the kitchen table. {love_interest} wants to talk before anyone signs anything, and for the first time in months, neither of you is angry.

choices.label: Sign it, and be kind
choices.result: You sign it together and make the hard parts fair: the house, the holidays, the friends. It hurts for a long time, {parent} calls every night that month, and you're proud of how you did it.

choices.label: Fight over everything
choices.result: Every chair, every account, every weekend becomes a fight through lawyers. It takes a year, costs a fortune and leaves you both strangers who used to be married.

choices.label: Ask for one more try
choices.result: One more try, you ask, with a counselor and no secrets. {love_interest} takes a long breath and agrees to six months. The papers go back in the drawer.

scenarios.title: The Investigation
scenarios.text: Two investigators from the league office are waiting in the general manager's conference room with a thick folder and a recorder, and they've asked for you by name.

choices.label: Tell them everything
choices.result: Everything, start to finish, and then your signature on the statement. The suspension is long, and the investigators write that you cooperated fully, which matters later more than you know.

choices.label: Bring a lawyer and say little
choices.result: A lawyer beside you, and as few words as possible. It drags out for weeks, every word is careful, and the suspension lands anyway, slightly longer.

choices.label: Deny it
choices.result: You deny it, even with the phone records on the table in front of you. The suspension is the longest the league gives, and the whole locker room reads about it on the same morning.

choices.label: Call {parent} that night
choices.result: You cooperate, and then you call {parent} that night and tell the whole story. It's the hardest call you've made, and {parent} stays on the line until you're ready to sleep.

scenarios.title: The Business Grows
scenarios.text: The start-up you backed for a friend is opening offices in three cities, and the founders want your face on the launch: billboards, a video, and a speech at the opening party.

choices.label: Do the launch
choices.result: You do the billboards, the video and the speech, with a lot of practice in the mirror. The launch is a success, your friend hugs you on stage, and your phone fills up with offers.

choices.label: Stay a silent investor
choices.result: You stay a silent investor and let the founders be the faces. It's their company and their moment, and they respect you more for knowing it.

choices.label: Ask for a seat at the table
choices.result: An advisory seat instead of a billboard is what you ask for. The meetings are long and interesting, and you learn more about business in a year than in your whole career.

scenarios.title: The Partner Who Cheats You
scenarios.text: Your accountant calls on a Sunday, which never happens. Your partner in the dealership has been cooking the books for a year, and some of the money missing has your name on the paperwork.

choices.label: Go to the police
choices.result: You go to the police on Monday with the accountant and every document. It's slow and public and humiliating, and it's the only way your name comes out clean.

choices.label: Settle it quietly
choices.result: You settle it quietly through the lawyers and take the loss. Nobody outside the family hears about it, and you lie awake for weeks doing sums in the dark.

choices.label: Confront your partner
choices.result: You drive to your partner's house and confront them on the porch. They cry and apologize and promise to pay it back, and you never see a cent of it.

choices.label: Call your advisor
choices.result: Your advisor has a plan before you've finished the first sentence: freeze the accounts, call the lawyer, call the police. It's still a bad month, and it's a contained one.
choices.lock_text: with an honest advisor in your corner

scenarios.title: A Franchise Offer
scenarios.text: A restaurant chain offers you a franchise with your name on it: real professionals running it this time, a real contract, and your face on the menu.

choices.label: Do it with professionals
choices.result: Signed, with professionals running it and two lawyers reading everything first. It opens in March, and the burger named after you is surprisingly good.

choices.label: Bring family in
choices.result: {sibling}, brought in to keep an eye on things for you. It's a family project now, and {sibling} turns out to be good at it.

choices.label: Stay out of restaurants
choices.result: No franchise for you. You have enough to think about already, and you've watched what restaurants did to two teammates' savings accounts.

scenarios.title: Selling the Business
scenarios.text: Someone wants to buy what you built, for more than you ever made kicking. The offer is on your kitchen table in a blue folder, and the buyer wants an answer by Friday.

choices.label: Sell it
choices.result: You sign on Friday, after one long night of reading every page. It feels strange to let it go, and also very light, like setting down a bag you'd stopped noticing.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.result: You keep it, because it's yours and it means something to the people who work there. The buyer is surprised, the staff are relieved, and you go back to work on Monday.

choices.label: Sell part and stay on
choices.result: You sell a share and stay on to run it, with a partner who knows more than you do. It's a compromise, and it gives the thing you built room to grow.

scenarios.title: The Business Shortcut
scenarios.text: Your business is losing money, and your partner has a way to make the books look better before the bank's review: two invoices, a little creative timing, and nobody gets hurt.

choices.label: Refuse and call the accountant
choices.result: No, and a call to your accountant that afternoon. The bank review is painful and honest, and the loan survives with tougher terms.

choices.label: Close the business clean
choices.result: The business, closed cleanly, with every bill paid and every employee given a reference. It's a loss, and you can look everyone in the eye.

choices.label: Sign the invoices
choices.result: The two invoices, signed at your partner's kitchen table. The bank is satisfied for a year, until an auditor notices the dates and calls your agent before he calls you.

scenarios.title: Betting to Cover It
scenarios.text: Your savings are thinner than anyone knows: an investment gone wrong, a house you can't sell, a payment due in March. An old acquaintance from home calls with an answer: one good week of bets, through him, and the hole closes.

choices.label: Hang up and call your advisor
choices.result: You hang up and call your advisor the same hour. The plan is slow and humbling, the house goes on the market at a loss, and you sleep for the first time in weeks.

choices.label: Tell {parent} how bad it is
choices.result: {parent} drives four hours that night and sits at your kitchen table with a calculator and a pot of coffee. By morning there's a plan, and you're not alone with it.

choices.label: Sell the thing you love
choices.result: The car you bought with your first big check goes to a dealer for less than it's worth. It stings every time you pass one like it, and the March payment is covered.

choices.label: Give him the money and the games
choices.result: The money and the names of three games go to him, none of them yours. For a month it works. Then the league's investigators find the account, and the commissioner's letter says a full season.

scenarios.title: The Insurance Claim
scenarios.text: Your agent suggests an insurance claim on a hamstring injury that's mostly healed: a doctor he knows, a form, and a payout that would cover two years of your kids' school.

choices.label: Refuse and change agents
choices.result: No, and you start looking for a new agent the same week. It's awkward and costly, and you sleep fine.

choices.label: Ask the union's lawyer
choices.result: The union's lawyer, asked quietly what the agent is suggesting. She explains exactly what it is, and you thank her and never mention it again.

choices.label: File the claim
choices.result: The form, signed in the agent's office. The payout comes in March; the investigators come in June, with questions about the doctor and a copy of your practice schedule.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Hearing
scenarios.text: Another hearing, years after the first one, and the union lawyer is younger than your snapper. The league's letter says it plainly: a veteran with your experience should have known better.

choices.label: Accept it without appeal
choices.result: Four games, no appeal. You practice with the scout team every day of it, early, and the young players notice how a veteran takes his punishment.

choices.label: Fight it
choices.result: You appeal and say the league is making an example of an old player. The appeal fails, the suspension doubles to eight games, and the story follows you to every road city.

choices.label: Accept it, and talk to the rookies
choices.result: Four games, accepted, and you ask the club to let you speak to the rookies about what it cost. The room is very quiet, and two of them thank you privately.

scenarios.title: Family Reunion, Pro Edition
scenarios.text: The family reunion, at a lake. Everyone wants a photo with you, an aunt wants your autograph for her mail carrier, and one uncle wants a loan for a boat.

choices.label: Take every photo
choices.result: Every photo, every autograph, and a promise to the uncle that you'll think about it. It's exhausting and warm, and {parent} beams all day.

choices.label: Say no to the loan kindly
choices.result: No to the boat, kindly and clearly. The uncle sulks through dessert, and three cousins thank you privately for saying it.

choices.label: Leave early
choices.result: An early exit, before the speeches. You'll see everyone next time, and {sibling} texts you a photo of the uncle's face.

scenarios.title: A Midnight Call From an Old Teammate
scenarios.text: A teammate from your rookie year calls at midnight. He's broke, the house is gone, and he doesn't know who else to call. He apologizes four times before he says why.

choices.label: Help him get back up
choices.result: A plan, not a check: an advisor you trust, a job interview with a friend, a loan for the first three months. He's on his feet by summer.

choices.label: Send what he needs tonight
choices.result: The money he needs, sent before you hang up. He cries on the phone, and you don't ask when he'll pay it back.

choices.label: Listen, and point him to help
choices.result: An hour of listening, and the number for the union's assistance program. It's the right help, and you wonder afterward if it was enough.

scenarios.title: The Big Second Contract
scenarios.text: Your agent says this is the contract that matters, the one that sets the rest of your life, and the club agrees, eventually, after a month of silence.

choices.label: Hold firm for your number
choices.result: Three tense weeks of holding firm. You get your number, and lose some sleep getting it, and the general manager doesn't smile at you for a while.

choices.label: Take the fair deal early
choices.result: A fair deal, taken early, and you stop thinking about it entirely. Your agent calls it smart, and means it, and you sleep well all spring.

choices.label: Decide it at home
choices.result: The decision, made at home, at the kitchen table. The number matters less than you thought, and you sign happily.

scenarios.title: The First Endorsement
scenarios.text: A local car wash offers you your first sponsorship: a billboard by the highway, four appearances in a giant foam sponge costume and a check that's small, but yours.

choices.label: Sign with the car wash
choices.result: The billboard goes up by the highway a week later, a little blurry, and every teammate sends you a photo of it. The holder sets it as his phone background.

choices.label: Ask your agent first
choices.result: Your agent negotiates the appearances down to two and the check up by half. The owner still makes you wear the sponge costume once, and you secretly love it.

choices.label: Keep your weeks clear
choices.result: No billboard, no sponge suit, no appearances. Your weeks stay clear for kicking, your account stays the same, and the car wash signs a local weatherman instead.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Request
scenarios.text: {best_friend} calls from home on a Sunday night and asks you for money. It's quiet for a long time before they ask, and you can hear how much it costs them to say it.

choices.label: Send it that night
choices.result: The money is in {best_friend}'s account before you hang up, and you never ask what it's for. They cry on the phone, and so, after the call, do you.

choices.label: Ask what it's for
choices.result: It's rent, three months behind. Paying the landlord directly makes both of you feel better, and {best_friend} sends you a photo of the receipt with a heart on it.

choices.label: Say no kindly
choices.result: No, as kindly as you can manage. It's true and it isn't, and the next phone call with {best_friend} is shorter, and the one after that doesn't come.

scenarios.title: The Equipment Upgrade
scenarios.text: A sales rep corners you after practice with expensive training equipment: a sensor suit, a kicking machine, and an app that charts every kick you've ever taken. He has a tablet and a very good smile.

choices.label: Buy the full setup
choices.result: All of it, delivered Thursday. The data is incredible, your living room is full of machines, and the bill is the kind you read twice.

choices.label: Use what the club has
choices.result: The club's staff charts you with what they already have. It's less fancy and nearly as good, and the trainer likes being asked.

choices.label: Keep it simple
choices.result: Your leg doesn't need an app, you decide. The rep leaves his card, your weeks stay simple, and you never think about sensor suits again.

scenarios.title: The Family Expectations
scenarios.text: Your family expects more now that you're earning. Cousins call about cars, an uncle about a boat, and {parent} about a roof that's been leaking since you were in high school.

choices.label: Set a family budget
choices.result: A yearly amount for family help, set at the kitchen table with {parent}. It's an awkward hour, and it ends the guessing, and the cousins stop calling about cars.

choices.label: Say yes to everything
choices.result: Yes to every request. It feels wonderful for a month, and your account feels it much longer, and nobody says thank you for the third one.

choices.label: Say not yet
choices.result: A rookie contract isn't forever money, you explain, as patiently as you can. Some of them understand. {sibling} doesn't, and says something you'll both remember.

scenarios.title: The Unexpected Bill
scenarios.text: Your car's transmission dies the week before a road trip, in the facility parking lot, in front of the whole offensive line. The repair costs more than the car is worth.

choices.label: Fix it
choices.result: Repaired, and a week of buses to practice in the meantime. The veterans think it's hilarious and start leaving bus schedules in your locker.

choices.label: Buy something new
choices.result: A brand-new car the same afternoon. It's lovely, it smells incredible, and the payment is going to follow you around for years.

choices.label: Ride with a teammate
choices.result: Rides with a teammate until you figure it out, and the drives turn into the best part of your week. By the time your car is fixed, you're friends.

scenarios.title: The Charity Donation
scenarios.text: Your aunt calls from home: the church you grew up in needs a new roof, and she's sure you'll want to help. She has already told the whole congregation you're thinking about it.

choices.label: Give generously
choices.result: More than she asked. The church puts your name on a brass plaque by the door, which you'll be embarrassed by forever, and {parent} visits it every Sunday.

choices.label: Give what you planned
choices.result: The amount in your budget, with an explanation. She's a little disappointed and grateful anyway, and the roof gets fixed by spring.

choices.label: Run a fundraiser at home
choices.result: A fundraiser in your hometown, run with {sibling}, raises twice the money with your time instead of your account. The whole town shows up.

scenarios.title: The First Big Purchase
scenarios.text: You can finally afford the car you've wanted since you were fifteen, the one on the poster above your childhood bed. The dealer already knows your name when you walk in.

choices.label: Buy it and drive it home
choices.result: Bought, and driven straight home to {parent}'s driveway. He walks around it three times without speaking, then asks for the keys.

choices.label: Buy something sensible
choices.result: Something sensible, with good mileage, and the rest goes in the bank. It's a good car. It isn't the car, and you notice every time you see one.

choices.label: Wait one more year
choices.result: A year's wait, on purpose. The wanting fades a little, and so does the fun of it, and you're not sure whether that's wisdom or a loss.

scenarios.title: The Regional Endorsement
scenarios.text: A regional grocery chain offers you a sponsorship worth more than your whole rookie salary: commercials, store openings, your face on cereal boxes in three states.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: Signed. The shoots take some weekends, the money is real, and {sibling} buys forty boxes of cereal with your face on them.

choices.label: Strike two clauses first
choices.result: The fine print, read twice, and two clauses struck: no appearances in season, no exclusivity. They agree, and you keep your Tuesdays.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: A pass, and your weekends stay yours. A rival kicker takes the deal, and you see his face in every aisle for a year.

scenarios.title: The Investment Pitch
scenarios.text: A man at a charity dinner pitches you an investment: guaranteed returns, a famous partner, no risk. He's done this before, and he knows you can tell.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: You thank him and walk away. Six months later you read his name in the paper, and you pass the article to your teammates.

choices.label: Ask someone you trust
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust. They laugh, then explain exactly how it works. You learn more in an hour than in a year of statements.

choices.label: Put money in
choices.result: You put money in. The statements look great for a while, then they stop coming, and so does he. The shame lasts longer than the loss.

scenarios.title: The First Home Repair
scenarios.text: The roof leaks the week of a road trip, all over the living room, and the repair estimate is the size of a used car. You're in a hotel two thousand miles away.

choices.label: Handle it from the hotel
choices.result: Contractors, insurance and photos, all handled by phone from the hotel. It gets done, expensively, and you miss a meeting doing it.

choices.label: Ask {parent} to oversee it
choices.result: {parent} drives over with a ladder and an opinion, and oversees the whole repair. He loves being useful, and the roof is perfect.

choices.label: Patch it for now
choices.result: A tarp and a bucket for now, the real fix in the offseason. It's cheap, and you sleep under the sound of dripping all winter.

scenarios.title: The Financial Mistake
scenarios.text: An investment you were sure about turns out not to be smart: a restaurant that closed, a fund that froze, a statement you read three times in the car outside the facility.

choices.label: Cut the loss
choices.result: The loss, cut cleanly, and a lesson learned. It stings for a month, and then it becomes a story you tell rookies.

choices.label: Tell {parent} everything
choices.result: Everything, at the kitchen table, including the part you were embarrassed about. It's a hard talk and a good one, and you make the next decision together.

choices.label: Bury it in work
choices.result: Work, to forget it: early mornings, long sessions, no thinking. It doesn't quite work, and the statement is still in the glove box.

choices.label: Call the advisor you trust
choices.result: The one advisor who has always told you the truth gets a call that afternoon. You make a plan together, you stick to it, and the hole closes by spring.
choices.lock_text: having learned about money the hard way

scenarios.title: The Family Business
scenarios.text: A cousin wants your money and your name to expand the family store into three towns. The whole family is waiting for your answer, and Thanksgiving is in two weeks.

choices.label: Invest
choices.result: You invest and put your name on the sign. The opening is a family party, and for the first time in years, everyone is in one room.

choices.label: Invest, quietly
choices.result: You put in money but keep your name off the sign. It's safer, and your cousin is a little hurt by the distance.

choices.label: Turn the cousin down
choices.result: No, as kindly and clearly as you can manage. Thanksgiving is quieter this year, and you're sure it was the right answer, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Memorabilia Deal
scenarios.text: A memorabilia collector wants to pay you to sign five hundred footballs in one afternoon, in a hotel ballroom, with a man counting and a camera to prove each one is real.

choices.label: Sign all five hundred
choices.result: Five hundred signatures in one long afternoon. Your hand hurts for days, the check is large, and the man counting never smiles once.

choices.label: Add a hundred for charity
choices.result: All five hundred, plus a hundred extra for the children's hospital auction. The auction raises more than your check, and the collector pays for the extra hundred.

choices.label: Sign for kids at the fence
choices.result: No ballroom, no counting man. You'd rather sign for kids at the practice fence, for free, and you do, every Thursday.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Savings
scenarios.text: A financial advisor reviews your long-term plan and asks a question you can't answer: what does your life cost after football, per year, in today's money?

choices.label: Learn the answer
choices.result: The answer, learned over two weeks of spreadsheets, and the next ten questions too. You understand your own money for the first time, and it's calming.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the next meeting
choices.result: {parent} comes to the next meeting with a legal pad and better questions than yours. You make the plan together, and he insists on paying for lunch.

choices.label: Trust the advisor
choices.result: The advisor knows best, you decide, and stop asking questions. It's easy and restful, and you never learn the number.

scenarios.title: The Personal Trainer
scenarios.text: A private trainer who works with three Olympic athletes could change your whole offseason, for a price that makes your advisor wince. They have one opening.

choices.label: Hire the trainer
choices.result: Hired, for the summer. It's brutal and scientific, and you come back to camp faster, leaner and slightly afraid of the trainer.

choices.label: Ask for a trial week
choices.result: A trial week first. It's good, so you hire them for half the summer, and keep the other half for your own work.

choices.label: Train the way you always have
choices.result: Your own routine, the one that got you here. It's familiar and cheaper, and you wonder all summer what you're missing.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Plan
scenarios.text: You sit down at the kitchen table with a calculator and a yellow pad and try to work out how much you'll need after football. The number is bigger than you expected.

choices.label: Do the math
choices.result: The math, done properly with an honest advisor over three meetings. It's sobering and useful, and you finally know what 'enough' looks like.

choices.label: Do it with {parent}
choices.result: {parent} sits beside you with a second calculator and decades of experience. You make the plan together, and it's better for it.

choices.label: Leave it for next year
choices.result: Next year, you decide, and the yellow pad goes in a drawer. The number keeps growing in your head anyway.

scenarios.title: The Expensive Lifestyle
scenarios.text: Your household's expenses have quietly doubled in two years: a second car, a bigger house, three subscriptions to things nobody watches, and a gardener for a garden you never visit.

choices.label: Cut back together
choices.result: An evening with the statements and a highlighter. Some things go, and nobody misses them, and the household feels lighter.

choices.label: Make a plan at home
choices.result: The plan, made at home, out loud, with everyone in the house. It's an awkward talk and a relief, and the budget goes on the fridge.

choices.label: Let it ride for now
choices.result: Later, you'll deal with it later. The statements keep coming, a little bigger each month, and you stop opening them on Mondays.

scenarios.title: The Advisor's Concern
scenarios.text: Your financial advisor slides one line of your statement across the table and asks, carefully, whether you still want to be in it. It's the investment a teammate talked you into.

choices.label: Listen and adjust
choices.result: You listen, ask the questions you skipped the first time, and move most of the money out. It costs you a little, and you sleep better.

choices.label: Get a second opinion
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust before deciding. They read it twice, sigh, and explain the part you didn't understand. You get out together.

choices.label: Keep it
choices.result: It stays in your portfolio. You like the idea and the teammate, and you tell yourself the advisor is being careful. The statements keep arriving.

scenarios.title: The Family Financial Decision
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} disagree about a major purchase: a lake house, two hours away, that one of you loves and the other thinks you'll never use.

choices.label: Let {love_interest} decide
choices.result: Their decision, fully. It's the right call, and you know it the first weekend you sit on the dock together.

choices.label: Sleep on it for a month
choices.result: A month, before anyone decides anything at all. The decision makes itself in the end, and neither of you has to win the argument.

choices.label: Make your case
choices.result: Your case, made carefully at the kitchen table with a spreadsheet and a chart. You win, and the house is very quiet for a whole day.

scenarios.title: The Old Teammate's Request
scenarios.text: A former teammate is starting a business and asks you to back him. He's earnest, he's prepared, and he's never run anything in his life.

choices.label: Back it with conditions
choices.result: You back it with conditions, a lawyer and a quarterly meeting. He grumbles about the paperwork and thanks you for it later.

choices.label: Back him fully
choices.result: You back him fully, because he's your friend. It's a risk, and he calls after every small win like a kid with a report card.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: You say no, kindly. He understands, mostly, and you both pretend at the next reunion that it didn't change anything.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Discount
scenarios.text: The club asks you to take less to stay, a lot less, because 'you're family here'. The general manager says it twice and puts a hand on your shoulder the second time.

choices.label: Take the discount
choices.result: The discount, accepted, because you want to finish here. The locker room notices, and so does the front office, and it feels right most days.

choices.label: Counter with a fair number
choices.result: A counter, fair and calm, through your agent. They meet you two-thirds of the way, and you sign without hard feelings.

choices.label: Look elsewhere
choices.result: Elsewhere, then. You thank them sincerely and start packing your locker in your head, and two clubs call by the end of the week.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Savings Review
scenarios.text: You go over your finances again with your advisor, but this time the question is different. Not 'how much can I spend', but 'how long does this have to last'.

choices.label: Plan for forty years
choices.result: Forty years, planned on a long spreadsheet with the advisor. It's sobering, and for the first time the numbers feel like a life, not a score.

choices.label: Bring {love_interest} in
choices.result: {love_interest} at the table, with their own questions, which are better than yours. You leave with a plan you both believe.
choices.lock_text: with someone at home to plan with

choices.label: Trust the plan you have
choices.result: The plan you already have, trusted for another year. Your advisor nods, mostly satisfied, and schedules a careful check-in for next spring, in pencil.

scenarios.title: The Business Offer
scenarios.text: A former teammate offers you a role in his business after football: a gym chain, three locations, a partner's title. He wants your name now and your time later.

choices.label: Join as a partner
choices.result: A partner, with your name on the door. The gyms do well, and you spend your Tuesdays learning about payroll.

choices.label: Invest quietly
choices.result: Money, but no name and no title on anything. It's safer, and your old teammate understands, mostly, after a long lunch.

choices.label: Say not yet
choices.result: After football, you tell him, you'll talk properly. He says the offer stands, and you believe him completely, and you shake on it.

scenarios.title: After Football, in the Family Firm
scenarios.text: Your family wants you in the family business after football: the hardware store {parent} built, three towns now, with a desk already set up with your name on it.

choices.label: Say yes for after
choices.result: Yes, for after football. {parent} cries on the phone, and you start learning the business on Tuesday mornings in the offseason.

choices.label: Invest, but don't work there
choices.result: Money to expand, but your own path after football. The family understands, mostly, and the store grows to four towns.

choices.label: Say you don't know yet
choices.result: Honestly, you don't know yet, you tell them. The desk stays right there, waiting, and {sibling} jokes at every holiday about taking it over.

scenarios.title: The Investment Decision
scenarios.text: Your advisor brings a proposal: a large investment in your life after football, a training facility with your name on it, a business you'd run when your leg finally says no.

choices.label: Build the facility
choices.result: The facility, built over two years, with a kicking field and a gym and your name over the door. It's the biggest bet you've ever made, and it feels like a future.

choices.label: Start smaller
choices.result: Something smaller first: two clinics a summer, rented fields, a real waiting list. If it works, you'll build; if not, you'll have learned cheaply.

choices.label: Keep your money safe
choices.result: Safe, for now, where it is. Your advisor agrees, a little disappointed, and the idea stays on a napkin in your desk drawer.

scenarios.title: The Financial Freedom Question
scenarios.text: A financial planner asks the question across a small round table, with a folder of charts open between you: do you have enough to stop? You realize you've never actually asked it out loud.

choices.label: Go through every number
choices.result: Every account, every debt, every promise to family, gone through line by line for three hours. The answer is clearer than you feared, and you drive home thinking about it.

choices.label: Ask {sibling} to sit in
choices.result: You ask {sibling} to sit in, because they're better with money than you'll ever be. They ask the hard questions, and the planner is visibly relieved.

choices.label: Put it off another season
choices.result: Another season first, you tell the planner, and close the folder. The question follows you home anyway, and you lie awake with it longer than you'd admit.

choices.label: Show the planner the old savings
choices.result: The planner opens the account you set up years ago and goes quiet, then laughs. You have more than enough, it turns out, because a younger you was careful.

scenarios.title: Partners in Something New
scenarios.text: A former teammate wants you as a partner in something new: a sports-performance gym in a strip mall, with his savings, your name on the sign, and a business plan printed at a copy shop.

choices.label: Go in as a partner
choices.result: You go in as a partner, with lawyers, a real contract and an accountant. The gym opens in the spring, and the sign with your name on it is slightly crooked.

choices.label: Lend your name only
choices.result: Your name on the sign, and nothing else: no money, no decisions. He's disappointed, then grateful, and the gym does fine without you worrying about it.

choices.label: Say no kindly
choices.result: No, kindly, over a long lunch: you're not ready for the next thing yet. He understands, and asks again a year later, and you're glad he did.

choices.label: Check everything first
choices.result: You've been cheated by a partner before, so you check everything: his books, his lease, his references. It all holds up, and you sign with a clear head.
choices.lock_text: having been cheated by a business partner

scenarios.title: Opening an Academy
scenarios.text: You've been thinking about opening a kicking academy for kids: a field, a few coaches, and a program for the ones who can't afford private lessons. A realtor has found you a field with a broken scoreboard.

choices.label: Buy the field
choices.result: You buy the field, fix the scoreboard and hire two coaches. The first summer camp has forty kids, half of them on scholarships, and the noise is wonderful.

choices.label: Start small, rent first
choices.result: A rented field on Sundays first, and a single coach. It's small and it works, and you learn what an academy actually needs before spending anything.

choices.label: Wait until you're done playing
choices.result: Not yet: an academy deserves your full attention, and you don't have it to give. You write the plan down and put it in a drawer to wait for you.

choices.label: Write the rules first
choices.result: You write the academy's rules first, about money, recruiters and honesty, because you've seen what happens without them. Parents notice, and the waiting list fills.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Financial Plan
scenarios.text: Your accountant wants to start moving your finances toward life after football: fewer risks, more savings, a plan that assumes the paychecks stop. There's a spreadsheet with three tabs labeled 'soon'.

choices.label: Make the plan now
choices.result: The plan, made now, tab by tab, over three long afternoons. It's dull and important, and when it's done you feel a weight lift that you hadn't known you were carrying.

choices.label: Keep one risk
choices.result: One risk kept on purpose: the business idea you've been sitting on for years. The accountant sighs and builds a safe plan around it, and you're grateful.

choices.label: Hand it to someone you trust
choices.result: You hand the whole thing to {sibling}, who has a head for numbers and a lot of patience. They do it better than you would have, and tease you about it forever.

choices.label: Discover you're already there
choices.result: The accountant runs the numbers twice and looks up: you're already there, because you lived small for all those years. You drive home in your old car, laughing.

scenarios.title: The Legacy Foundation
scenarios.text: You've been thinking about a foundation for young athletes from families like yours: equipment, camp fees, rides to practice. A lawyer has sent the paperwork, and the first page asks for a name.

choices.label: Name it after your first coach
choices.result: You name it after your first coach, who cries on the phone when you tell them. The first fifty kids get cleats and camp fees by summer.

choices.label: Start it quietly
choices.result: No name on the door and no gala: just checks for camp fees, sent quietly to coaches who know which kids need them. Nobody knows it's you, which is the point.

choices.label: Wait until you retire
choices.result: Not yet: a foundation deserves your full attention. You file the paperwork in a drawer labeled 'after', and it waits there patiently.

choices.label: Write the rules about money first
choices.result: You write strict rules first, about who can give and what they get, because you once refused help that came with strings. The coaches trust it immediately.
choices.lock_text: having refused improper help in college

scenarios.title: The Retirement Financial Review
scenarios.text: Your financial advisor wants to review whether you're ready to stop: one meeting, every account, and a single question at the end that she's written in capital letters at the top of the page.

choices.label: Answer the question honestly
choices.result: Every account opened, every number read aloud, and at the end you answer her question honestly. The answer is yes, and hearing it said frightens and frees you at once.

choices.label: Bring {sibling}
choices.result: {sibling} comes along, because they ask better questions than you do. The meeting runs long, and {sibling} takes notes that you'll use for years.

choices.label: Postpone the meeting
choices.result: Postponed, for a season, with an apology. The question waits in your inbox, polite and patient, and you think about it every time you see the envelope icon.

choices.label: Laugh at the answer
choices.result: She runs the numbers and laughs, because a younger you was so careful there's nothing to worry about. You drive home lighter than you've felt in years.

scenarios.title: The Meal Money
scenarios.text: The per diem envelope on the first road trip is thicker than any scholarship check you ever got in college. The veterans are already planning where theirs is going tonight.

choices.label: Put it in the bank
choices.result: The whole envelope goes in the bank, and you eat the team meals. By December the road trips have quietly paid for your offseason trainer.

choices.label: Take the rookies out
choices.result: The rookie class eats like kings for one night on your envelope. It's gone by dessert, and four rookies will remember it for years.

choices.label: Treat yourself, a little
choices.result: A good dinner alone, a good book from the airport and a long nap. It feels like being a grown-up, and you send {parent} a photo of the dessert.

scenarios.title: Rookie Year Taxes
scenarios.text: Your first tax bill as a pro arrives in a thick envelope: a number nobody prepared you for, due in a month, with forms from every state you played a road game in.

choices.label: Hire an athletes' accountant
choices.result: An accountant who only works with athletes takes the whole envelope off your hands. It's done in two weeks, correctly, and you learn what a 'jock tax' is.

choices.label: Ask a veteran at lunch
choices.result: One veteran at lunch gives you his accountant's number and a story about his first year that makes you laugh until your stomach hurts.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.result: A long weekend with spreadsheets and coffee. It's stressful, probably right, and you feel strangely proud when you click the last button.

scenarios.title: Free Cleats
scenarios.text: A shoe company offers you free cleats and a small contract, if you wear them on camera. The cleats are bright orange, and your old pair has been with you since college.

choices.label: Sign and lace up
choices.result: Signed, and the orange cleats arrive the next day. They're fine, the check pays for your offseason training, and the veterans call you 'traffic cone'.

choices.label: Test them for a week
choices.result: A week of testing before you sign anything. They're good, so you sign, with a clause that lets you wear your old pair if they ever hurt.

choices.label: Keep your old cleats
choices.result: Your old cleats stay. Your feet are happy and your account is the same, and the equipment manager pats them like an old dog.

scenarios.title: The Card Signing
scenarios.text: A trading card company wants your signature on a thousand cards in one afternoon, in a hotel conference room with bad coffee and a man counting.

choices.label: Sign all thousand
choices.result: A thousand signatures in four hours. Your hand hurts for two days, the check is nice, and your signature gets worse with every hundred.

choices.label: Sign some for charity
choices.result: Two hundred cards, and a full set donated to a children's hospital raffle. The raffle raises more than the check would have.

choices.label: Pass on the cards
choices.result: No cards this time. Your hand is grateful, and the company signs a punter instead, who sends you a smug photo of his check.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Payday Dinner
scenarios.text: Your rookie class decides to celebrate your first full paychecks together at a restaurant you can't pronounce, with a menu that doesn't have prices on it.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: The whole night, every course. The bill is absurd, the night is worth it, and you all take a photo with the chef.

choices.label: Suggest a cheaper place
choices.result: A cheaper place with the same view, you suggest. Half the class comes, the rest think you're cheap, and your half has more fun.

choices.label: Order in
choices.result: Takeout, alone, on the couch. Your account is happier than you are, and you see the photos the next morning.

scenarios.title: Your First Credit Card Bill
scenarios.text: Your first credit card statement as a pro arrives, four pages long, and you don't remember half the charges. One of them is a subscription to a magazine about boats.

choices.label: Go through every line
choices.result: Every line, with a highlighter, at the kitchen table. Four subscriptions canceled, including the boat magazine, which you still don't remember ordering.

choices.label: Pay it and forget it
choices.result: Paid in full, and forgotten. The same thing happens next month, and the month after, with slightly different boats, and you stop opening the envelopes.

choices.label: Ask a veteran at lunch
choices.result: A veteran at lunch shows you the app he uses and his worst statement ever, which makes yours look like a grocery list. You laugh until it hurts.

scenarios.title: The Raise
scenarios.text: Your new contract is real money, and everyone you know has noticed: old friends with ideas, cousins with emergencies, a teacher from middle school with a fundraiser.

choices.label: Set one rule for everyone
choices.result: One rule, for everyone, written down. It's fair, it's a little lonely, and the calls slow down within a month.

choices.label: Help the ones who need it
choices.result: The people who really need it get help, quietly, and nobody else hears about it. {parent} finds out anyway and is proud.

choices.label: Change your number
choices.result: A new phone number, given to twelve people. Things get quieter immediately, and two old friends feel shut out and say so.

scenarios.title: The House With a Yard
scenarios.text: You buy a house with a backyard big enough for a kicking net. The previous owners left a swing set, a lemon tree and a note wishing you luck.

choices.label: Put up the net
choices.result: The net goes up the first weekend. The neighbors watch from their windows, and by Sunday their kids are shagging balls for you.

choices.label: Throw a housewarming
choices.result: Everyone, over, the first Saturday: family, teammates, neighbors. {parent} gives the tour twice, and {sibling} falls off the swing set.

choices.label: Sit under the lemon tree
choices.result: Nothing, in the backyard, under the lemon tree, for a whole afternoon. It's the first time in years you've done nothing on purpose.

scenarios.title: The Investment Club
scenarios.text: A group of teammates forms an investment club: monthly meetings, a shared account, a lot of opinions about technology stocks. They want you in, and the first meeting is at the quarterback's house.

choices.label: Join the club
choices.result: Joined. The meetings are mostly jokes and some good ideas, and the account does fine, and the friendships do better.

choices.label: Join with limits
choices.result: In, with a small amount and one rule: nothing you don't understand. You end up explaining index funds to a linebacker, who becomes your biggest convert.

choices.label: Keep money and friends apart
choices.result: Money and friends don't mix, for you. You stay out, politely, and still go to the meetings for the food.

scenarios.title: The Second Car
scenarios.text: You buy a second car on a whim after a good week, a convertible in a color the salesman called 'victory'. Then you realize you haven't driven the first one in a month.

choices.label: Sell one of them
choices.result: One of them goes back on the market by Friday, at a loss. You feel smarter for it, and a little silly every time you see a convertible.

choices.label: Give the old one to {sibling}
choices.result: The old car, keys and all, goes to {sibling}, who cries in the driveway and then honks the horn for ten straight seconds.

choices.label: Keep both cars
choices.result: Both stay. They sit side by side in the driveway, shining, and the insurance bill makes you laugh out loud in a bad way.

scenarios.title: The Mortgage
scenarios.text: Your first mortgage, and the papers are thicker than your playbook: forty pages of terms, a stack of signature tabs, and a loan officer who keeps calling you 'the athlete'.

choices.label: Read every page
choices.result: Every page, read, with questions about the three that matter. The loan officer is surprised and fixes one clause in your favor.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the signing
choices.result: {parent} at the signing, with reading glasses and opinions. He's done this before and asks the questions you didn't know to ask.

choices.label: Sign where they point
choices.result: Signed where they point, every tab, in twenty minutes. You hope for the best, and for a year you're never quite sure what you agreed to.

scenarios.title: The Brand Ambassador
scenarios.text: A sporting-goods brand wants you as its regional ambassador for three years: commercials, store openings, a signature cleat. The contract arrives with a pen taped to it.

choices.label: Sign for three years
choices.result: Three years, signed. It's steady money and a lot of store openings, and your signature cleat is ugly in a way you grow to love.

choices.label: Sign for one year
choices.result: One year, with an option for more. They agree, a little surprised, and you keep your freedom for the next negotiation and the one after.

choices.label: Pass on the cleat
choices.result: No contract. Three years is a long time, and the cleat really is ugly. A rival kicker signs instead, and you see his face at the mall.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Clinic Tour
scenarios.text: A kicking company wants you on a weekend clinic tour: eight cities, eight Saturdays, a thousand young kickers who all want to know what your secret is.

choices.label: Do the whole tour
choices.result: All eight cities. You see a thousand young kickers and remember being one, and you lose your voice in the sixth city.

choices.label: Do the dates near home
choices.result: The three dates near home, and your own training the rest of the time. It's a good balance, and the kids in your hometown are thrilled.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: No tour. Your weekends stay yours, and you spend them doing nothing much with the people you love most, which is the point.

scenarios.title: The Contract Bonus
scenarios.text: You hit a contract bonus on the last day of the season. Your agent calls to congratulate you and asks you, very seriously, to celebrate quietly.

choices.label: Put it all in savings
choices.result: The whole bonus, straight into savings, and you tell almost nobody about it. Your advisor sends a single word by text: 'Proud.'

choices.label: Treat the specialists
choices.result: A nice dinner for the specialists, on you, and nobody posts about it. {holder} gives a toast to 'the bonus we all earned'.

choices.label: Celebrate at home
choices.result: Takeout, a movie and a very long sleep at home. It's the quietest celebration in league history, and it's exactly right.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Account
scenarios.text: Your advisor finally gets you to open a retirement account, after three years of reminders. The paperwork is waiting on the table, with little yellow arrows.

choices.label: Do it right
choices.result: Done right: every arrow signed, every question asked, contributions set to grow on their own. Your advisor sends a photo of the paperwork, framed, as a joke.

choices.label: Ask {parent} what he wishes he'd done
choices.result: What does {parent} wish he'd done at your age? It's a long, honest talk on the phone, and it changes what you sign.

choices.label: Sign the minimum
choices.result: The minimum, signed and then forgotten about. Your advisor sighs on the phone and sets a reminder for the same day next year.

scenarios.title: The Second Business
scenarios.text: You're considering a second business while the first is still finding its feet: a gym this time, with your name on the door and a partner who talks very fast.

choices.label: Wait a year
choices.result: A year's wait, until the first business is steady. The fast-talking partner finds someone else, and you're relieved by spring.

choices.label: Do both
choices.result: Both, at once. You don't sleep much for months, and the gym opens in June to a line around the block.

choices.label: Ask your first partner
choices.result: Your partner in the first business, asked honestly over lunch. The answer is 'please not yet', and you listen to them.

scenarios.title: The Real Estate Pitch
scenarios.text: A real estate agent with very white teeth pitches you on rental properties over lunch. The numbers look great on her tablet, and she has a building in mind.

choices.label: Study the numbers
choices.result: You take the numbers home, study them for a week and buy one small building. It's work, and it's yours.

choices.label: Ask {parent}
choices.result: You ask {parent}, who has strong opinions about landlords and stronger ones about leaky roofs. You don't buy, and you learn a lot.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: You pass. You'd rather not fix anyone's sink, and the agent finds a linebacker by the end of the week.

scenarios.title: The Investment That Works
scenarios.text: An investment you made years ago, mostly to stop your advisor asking, has quietly turned into real money. Nobody knows about it but you and your advisor.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.result: You leave it alone and let it keep growing. It's the first time money has felt like a plan instead of a pressure.

choices.label: Share some of it
choices.result: You use some of it to clear a family debt nobody talks about. The call where you tell them is short, and nobody can speak at the end.

choices.label: Treat yourself once
choices.result: You treat yourself once, quietly: the watch you looked at for years. You wear it on game days and feel a little foolish and very happy.

scenarios.title: The Tax Audit
scenarios.text: You're audited, and every receipt from the last three years matters. A man in a gray suit wants to know about a dinner in 2023 that you don't remember at all.

choices.label: Hire an accountant
choices.result: A good accountant, hired that same afternoon. It's expensive and calm, and the man in the gray suit leaves satisfied.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.result: Every receipt, organized by you, every night for a month. You learn a great deal about your own life, some of it embarrassing.

choices.label: Sort receipts with {parent}
choices.result: {parent}, at the kitchen table, sorting receipts into shoeboxes with you for a week. He finds the 2023 dinner receipt in a coat pocket.

scenarios.title: The Public Speaking Gig
scenarios.text: A company wants you to give a motivational talk to two thousand employees in a convention center. The fee is large, and the topic is 'resilience'.

choices.label: Give a real talk
choices.result: A real talk, about failing in public and staying. They stand up at the end, and three people find you afterward to tell their own stories.

choices.label: Tell stories and laugh
choices.result: Funny stories, mostly about your own mistakes. They laugh a lot, and the CEO asks you back for next year.

choices.label: Turn the speech down
choices.result: Speeches aren't your thing, you decide, and you turn it down politely. They book an astronaut instead, who is much better.

scenarios.title: The Kids' Book
scenarios.text: A publisher wants you to write a children's book about learning to kick. The editor says to write it the way you'd tell it to a seven-year-old.

choices.label: Write it
choices.result: You write it at the kitchen table with {sibling}'s kids correcting every page. The dedication is to them, and they read it to their classes.

choices.label: Write it with {holder}
choices.result: You write it with {holder}, who insists on a chapter about the holder. It's funnier than the one you'd have written alone.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You pass for now and tell the editor maybe after football. You keep the email, and some nights you start a first line in your head.

scenarios.title: Three Possible Futures
scenarios.text: A retirement planner lays three futures on the table: retire now, retire in two years, or play until the body decides. Only one of them has football in it for long.

choices.label: Choose the two-year plan
choices.result: Two more years, planned in detail, with money set aside for the year after. It's the first time the end has felt like a place you can walk to.

choices.label: Take all three home
choices.result: All three futures, taken home and spread out on the dining table. Your family argues for a week and agrees on one.

choices.label: Keep playing and decide later
choices.result: Football, for as long as it lasts, and the planning later. The planner sighs and leaves the folder, just in case.

scenarios.title: The Last Big Endorsement
scenarios.text: A national sponsor offers what may be your last big deal: one season, a commercial, and a farewell campaign about longevity. The ads will have your face on every bus.

choices.label: Sign the farewell campaign
choices.result: Signed, with your face on every bus. The campaign is tasteful and kind, and strangers start telling you to keep going.

choices.label: Make it about the kids
choices.result: Your condition: half the campaign goes to your foundation's youth clinics. They agree, and the ads feature kids kicking instead of you.

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.result: No farewell campaign before you've actually decided to say farewell. The sponsor understands completely and leaves the door open for next year.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Minimum, Again
scenarios.text: Another season at the veteran minimum, the third in a row. The number is still more than most people make, and it's a long way from what you used to make.

choices.label: Be grateful out loud
choices.result: Grateful, out loud, at your locker and at home. A paycheck to kick a ball at your age is a gift, and saying it makes it feel like one.

choices.label: Tighten the budget
choices.result: A tighter budget, built with your advisor and your family. Nobody misses much, and {sibling} thinks the new rules are hilarious.

choices.label: Earn a raise
choices.result: A raise, earned the old way: the best season of your late career. Your agent has a reason to call the club in March.

scenarios.title: The Family Business Offer
scenarios.text: {sibling} wants you to join their business when you retire: a landscaping company with twelve trucks, a good name in town, and a sign they've already designed with both your names.

choices.label: Say yes, for after
choices.result: Yes, for after. {sibling} sends you a photo of the sign the same night, and you start learning the business on Mondays.

choices.label: Invest instead of joining
choices.result: Money for two more trucks, but your own path after football. {sibling} understands, and the trucks have your name on the door anyway.

choices.label: Tell them you need time
choices.result: Time, you tell {sibling} honestly over the phone. They say the sign isn't going anywhere, and neither are they, whatever you decide.
